title: Release surge priority matrix and comm window - May 2026 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures the preflight checklist, a surge-priority heatmap (who to ring during capacity/latency spikes), a short rollout calendar with tight timeboxes, and an initial draft of release notes for the May 2026 platform release. Designed for eng-release-engineering, SRE, serving-runtime, and oncall stakeholders.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Hosted API minor release + Dedicated config changes + console UX tweaks. No DB schema migrations.
- Audience: Release engineers, SREs, serving-runtime owners, product PM, solutions-eng oncall.

High-level goals:
- Ship feature toggles for model-routing policies with zero-customer-downtime.
- Ensure predictable latency SLOs during regional ramp.
- Establish clear comm windows and escalation paths for surge events.

Heatmap: surge-priority matrix (who to call first)
- P0 latency / outage (global): Pager to SRE oncall -> Release lead -> Platform infra manager -> Exec oncall
- P0 model-serving degradation (single-region): Pager to serving-runtime oncall -> Model infra lead -> Release engineer
- P1 elevated error rate (route-level): Slack #release-alerts + oncall -> owning-team engineer during business hours -> release engineer fallback at nights
- P2 non-urgent regressions: triage ticket in RL-3410 -> assignee within 48h

Contact routing and escalation windows (times in PDT):
- Preflight window (48h before cut): 09:00-17:00 daily - primary contact: release lead (Sofia Martinez)
- Cutover window: 23:00-02:00 (low-traffic target) - required attendees: release lead, serving-runtime oncall, infra oncall, SRE lead, product pm
- Post-cut validation: 02:00-06:00 - SLO watch and rollback guardrail active

Preflight checklist (ordered, must be ticked off before we greenlight):
- [ ] Finalize canary config and percent buckets in RL-3372
- [ ] Verify model catalog variant mapping + fallback policies are set in staging and mirrored in prod-config repo
- [ ] Run smoke generation test (10k tokens over 30m) against canary pool - observe p95/p99
- [ ] Confirm KV cache priming script ran for common prefixes (see linked script in PR 1284)
- [ ] Load test for expected QPS peak + 20% buffer for 1h - observe queue depth and GPU utilization
- [ ] Confirm autoscaling policies for Dedicated pools (min/max) are synced to infra manifests
- [ ] Validate log retention and trace sampling adjustments for this release on Console (temporary 48h high retention)
- [ ] Security scan completed for binary artifacts and container images (SCA report attached to CON-1421)
- [ ] Final rollout playbook published and shared to #release-ops with attendees list and phone tree
- [ ] Stakeholder comm blurb drafted and signed off by product and legal (see "Release comms" section below)

Cutover condensed timeline (timeboxes) - target weekend: 2026-05-23 to 2026-05-24
- 2026-05-23 20:00 PDT - Final freeze and last-minute hotfix cutoff
- 2026-05-23 22:30 PDT - Preflight smoke run and SLO baseline snapshot (automated)
- 2026-05-23 23:00 PDT - Canary rollout starts (5% traffic) -> step monitor for 20m
- 2026-05-24 00:00 PDT - Canary expansion to 20% -> monitor 30m (p95/p99, error rate)
- 2026-05-24 00:45 PDT - Canary expansion to 50% -> monitor 30m; if stable, plan full release
- 2026-05-24 01:30 PDT - Full release to 100% (or staged region-by-region depending on telemetry)
- 2026-05-24 02:15 PDT - Post-cut verification: traffic unit tests, sample queries validated, regression probe run
- 2026-05-24 03:30 PDT - Release lead signoff or rollback decision point

Rollback criteria (automatic or manual triggers):
- Automatic: sustained p99 latency > 2x baseline for 15 minutes OR error rate > 1% for 10 minutes on newly routed traffic -> automatic rollback to previous model variant
- Manual: any customer-impacting 5xx increase visible across >1 region or pipeline failure in batch tasks -> manual rollback by release lead after cross-team sync

Post-release validation list (first 24h):
- [ ] Validate telemetry: p50/p95/p99, error rates, tail-latency spikes per region
- [ ] Spot-check 50 customer journeys across most-used routes (random sample using probe harness)
- [ ] Check billing/usage counters for anomalies (unusual token inflation)
- [ ] Ensure fallback policies engage correctly for simulated capacity pressure
- [ ] Capture and file any small regressions (severity <= low) into RL-3410 for triage

Known risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Autoscaler misconfiguration leading to slow scale-up. Mitigation: pre-scale Dedicated pools during the canary window and enable temporary burst nodes.
- Risk: KV cache coldness causing initial latency spikes. Mitigation: run priming job and hold canary at 5% longer if first 20m shows cache churn.
- Risk: External dependency (third-party logging) delayed writes. Mitigation: run degraded-path tests and short-lived retention increase to reduce signal loss.

Stakeholder communications (blurb templates)
- External (customers): "We will be rolling a minor platform update on May 24 (00:00 PDT) which includes improved model-routing and performance fixes. There should be no disruption to normal usage; in the rare event of degradation, traffic will be rolled back automatically."
- Internal (all-hands via #release-ops): short timeline, expected impact, oncall phone tree, and link to live status page.

Release notes draft (talking points - internal draft)
- Highlights:
  - Model-routing policy: safer fallbacks and per-route routing weights (beta)
  - Performance: median generation latency down ~12% for short-form requests (internal benchmark)
  - Console: route-level latency breakdown added to per-route dashboard

- Bug fixes:
  - Fix: rare race in KV cache eviction that could cause transient 502s under bursty traffic (RL-3372)
  - Fix: serving runtime memory leak on 2.1.x path when KV cache disabled for large-context requests

- Operational notes for SRE/ops:
  - Default canary bucket sizes: 5%/20%/50%/100% (adjustable per region)
  - Autoscaler transient threshold lowered to reduce cold-start tail latency for models >8B
  - Temporary telemetry retention increased to 48h for the release window; revert back on May 28 unless extended

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Q1: Do we enable per-customer pinning by default for Dedicated customers in this release? (decision owner: product PM, deadline: 2026-05-10)
- Q2: Which regions should we roll sequentially vs parallel? (recommendation: parallel for NA regions, sequential for EU -> decision owner: infra lead)
- Q3: Approve the temporary retention bump to 48h for trace logs (security review required)

Action items (owner -> due):
- Ethan Park -> finish autoscaler manifest review (due 2026-05-10)
- Maya Chen -> finalize the canary traffic config and add to RL-3372 (due 2026-05-12)
- Arjun Patel -> run priming job and post results in CON-1421 (due 2026-05-18)
- Sofia Martinez -> publish signed release comms and phone-tree to #release-ops (due 2026-05-20)

Notes to self / draft chat copy (informal):
- "If p99 jumps but p50 does not, likely cold-cache - give canary extra 20m rather than rollback immediately."
- "Keep the phone tree compact; limit to 6 people for P0 to avoid coordination lag."

Appendix (quick links):
- Canary config PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-configs/pull/312
- Autoscaler change: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284
- Trace retention request: CON-1421

Status: draft. This is intended to be iterated in the drive and during the next release sync. Please add comments inline and update task owners when handing off.
